articles.title: Two days past Deepavali, NPCI yet to announce a date for UPI MDR rollout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Two days since Deepavali, the National Payments Council of India is yet to notify a new date for the implementation of the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions and The Hindu has learnt that “there is no announcement on this at the moment”.

When it had put the proposed additional charge on hold nearly a month ago, the NPCI had said the new date would be announced “immediately” after Deepavali. The new rate was originally supposed to have been implemented on October 15.
“There is no announcement on this at the moment,” a spokesperson at the NPCI told The Hindu when asked whether the NPCI’s date announcement was imminent.

The matter of an MDR levy on specified UPI transactions received significant pushback from merchants and petrol pump dealers alike, apart from customers who feared that merchants would pass on the extra charge on to them by way of higher prices.
The petrol pump dealers further said that the MDR charge, coupled with the fact that their dealer commission had not been revised in several years, meant that their margins would be further squeezed.

The NPCI had on October 13 announced that its UPI and Services Steering Committee had decided that “keeping in mind the festive season, Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions, shall be implemented immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately”.

The Hindu had at the time reported that, according to government sources, the decision to delay the implementation of MDR on UPI was made in the Prime Minister’s Office following strong appeals from traders.

Praveen Khandelwal, founder and secretary-general of the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) and a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Lok Sabha member, had welcomed the deferment, saying that it would protect traders’ interests and sustain digital payment momentum during the festive season.

articles.title: Moody’s ups India’s FY27 growth estimate to 7% on broad-based momentum
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Moody's Ratings on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) said the Indian economy is expected to grow at a higher rate of 7 per cent in the current fiscal, led by broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience.

In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, Moody's, however, said that near-term risks to growth persist as household consumption remains vulnerable to “intensifying and broadening price pressures”, with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 2-6% target range, while a deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions will weigh on agricultural output and rural demand.
“India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7% from 6.5%,” it said.
Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7% over the medium term, Moody's said.
A sustained private investment boom that materially boosts manufacturing, employment and productivity could lift growth rates above Moody's baseline projections.
“With the RBI on track to raise rates further, tighter monetary policy could delay the recovery in private investment,” Moody's added.

India has adjusted to the energy price shock better than previously assumed, helped by its ability to diversify crude and gas supplies and buffer consumers from the immediate price impact through state-backed oil marketing companies and tax cuts.

India is also home to the world's largest single-site refining complex, and its large and sophisticated refining capacity has helped limit fuel supply disruptions while supporting its role as a major exporter of refined petroleum products, Moody's added.

“High frequency indicators, including robust capital goods production and imports, accelerating industrial credit growth and rising capacity utilisation, suggest that India may be at the cusp of a new private capex cycle after several years of corporate and banking- sector balance sheet repair,” the U.S.-based agency said.

articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players.

“Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.”

The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.

One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

Industry experts also suggest that while amendments in tax laws are just one part of attracting inflows, what remains important is continued momentum in corporate earnings growth, policy certainty and a stable rupee.

As such, simplifying onboarding and setting one predictable tax clearance process at exit coupled with making dispute resolution faster and binding is what would bring stable long-term investments, Nangia noted.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine hold second day of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Delegations from Moscow and Kyiv on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) held a second straight day of U.S.-brokered talks on ways of ending the war started by Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.

Hopes are low for any breakthrough in the first meeting in nine months between the delegations, although U.S. officials say they are determined to revive peace efforts that so far have failed to deliver significant results.
“We are starting the second day of negotiations,” Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service who leads Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, said on social media.

The envoys met for four hours on Tuesday (November 10) in the capital of the United Arab Emirates, which was chosen as a neutral venue. The talks, mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff, were due to conclude later Wednesday (November 11).

The context of the negotiations has changed since the last meeting in February in Geneva. The Trump administration has to reckon with Democrats, who could demand more support for Ukraine, taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections.
Also, Russia's wartime economy is under heavy strain, and Ukraine is reeling from devastating aerial attacks on its power grid.
Mr. Umerov said that Wednesday (November 11) would begin with three-way talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States, with Kyiv's delegation meeting afterwards with European officials.
Moscow doesn't want European countries, which are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent, involved in the direct negotiations.
However, representatives of European governments, the European Union and NATO were in Abu Dhabi and were consulting with the Ukrainian delegation, officials said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday's (November 10) session was “constructive and quite substantive”.
The talks were largely about humanitarian issues, including possible prisoner exchanges and returning Ukrainian civilians in captivity, as well as children taken from the country, he said.
Security guarantees also were discussed, he said. However, Russia and Ukraine have shown no sign of a willingness to compromise on their demands.

articles.title: Pakistan Deputy PM Ishaq Dar's grandson, seven others indicted in Lahore gang rape case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A Pakistani court has indicted eight suspects, including the grandson of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, in a gang rape of two foreign women, an official said on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

"Lahore's Additional District & Sessions Judge (AD&SJ) Rafaqat Ali Gondal on Tuesday (November 10) framed charges against the suspects who pleaded not guilty," a court official said and added the judge directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on December 9 so that the formal trial proceedings could be commenced.
All the suspects, presently in judicial custody, were produced before the trial court for the indictment proceedings.
Ironically, Punjab police had already given a "clean chit" to Ishaq Dar's grandson Raza Dar and his four accomplices in this case.

Police not only absolved Dar's grandson and his four friends of rape charges but charged three other low-paid employees of him of raping the women, as per a police report earlier submitted in the court.

The two women, one from the Netherlands and the other from Venezuela, were allegedly kidnapped and raped by Raza Dar and four of his friends after arriving in Lahore on a business trip in June this year.
The medical examination confirmed that the foreign women were raped. Both victim women after recording their statements had left for their home countries.
According to the police report, the victim women said that they met Raza Dar in Singapore in 2025 and invited him to invest money with them in the business of crypto currency.
After getting profit returns on initial investment, Raza Dar invested over $500,000.

"However, this time, the women did not give any profit or return the amount to the suspect," the report said, adding in June this year, the suspect invited both women to Pakistan on the pretext of a meeting with another investor, where they stayed at a hotel in Islamabad and travelled to Murree hill station with their free will.
Later the women were taken to a house in Defence Housing Authority Lahore, where they were allegedly detained and pressured to pay the amount.

"The armed men guarded the women at the house, threatened them with a knife, a gun and a piece of broken mirror, and warned that they would be killed and their body parts sold if they failed to meet the demands," police said and added the women managed to escape when their kidnappers were taking them to Lahore airport and on the way their vehicle had an accident.

articles.title: Alice Huang, who reportedly had affair with Nvidia CEO, is Chinese banker turned tech exec
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: She was building a career in Chinese finance before turning to tech with a leadership role at a data centre company in Singapore. He is the high-profile CEO of Nvidia, the California-based company that makes computer chips relied upon by advanced artificial intelligence systems.
An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds.
The Chinese businesswoman also known as Huang Le had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, according to reports over the past month by the New York Times.

The newspaper also reported that top policymakers were informed in a memo that intelligence indicated she was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, recruited to influence Nvidia to make its most advanced chips more available in China.

In one widely shared photograph of the pair, Jensen Huang and people surrounding him are holding drinks in Taipei, while Alice Huang sits behind him, apparently watching him in conversation. The picture was posted in 2024 by software company NetThunder to its LinkedIn page.
It remains unclear how long the affair lasted, and when exactly the relationship might have ended. The Associated Press was unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.
Publicly available information about Alice Huang is scant.
She was a Chinese finance executive before becoming involved in artificial intelligence, data centres and computer chips.

In 2023, she became a director at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which describes itself as an “NVIDIA cloud partner”. Last year, Megaspeed faced scrutiny from the U.S. over its alleged skirting of U.S. export restrictions and routing of a large amount of advanced Nvidia chips for Chinese users.

Megaspeed was incorporated in 2015 in Singapore with the name 7Road International, after being spun off as the overseas arm of a Chinese video game developer, according to corporate registration records.
Filings show that in March 2023, it renamed itself Megaspeed International, with all of the shares transferred to Huang Le Limited, a company registered in the British Virgin Islands.
That same month, Alice Huang became Megaspeed's controlling shareholder, according to research by the C4ADS, a Washington-based nonprofit focused on global security.

articles.title: Spain’s first general strike in 14 years brings clashing social and political desires to the fore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Millions of Spain’s workers are striking on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) to demand that the government remedy the nation’s housing crisis less than three weeks before a national election that could catapult the far right to power.

Spain’s first general strike in 14 years is expected to cause delays to the widely used public transport system and lead to the slowdown or shuttering of businesses, factories and shops across the eurozone’s fourth largest economy.

Minor incidents were reported in the first hours, including roadblocks — some of them with burning tyres — in Barcelona, the second-largest city in the country, and scuffles between picketers and police near the country’s main wholesale market on the outskirts of the capital, Madrid. Striking workers set off fireworks on the stroke of midnight as they gathered in public squares in Barcelona.

The two main unions calling for the strike, UGT and CCOO, reported widespread participation in the early hours “with significant work stoppages in strategic sectors” — 90% in the automotive and port sectors, 85% in the meat industry, 82% in waste collection, and 75% in the energy sector — according to a statement posted on social media.
Between workers, activists, politicians and ordinary Spaniards, the groups have very different interests in Wednesday's (November 11) walkout.
The average rent in Spain has almost doubled in the last 10 years, eating into household budgets and angering voters.

Public anger over housing reached a boiling point following the nationally televised eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home in Madrid last month. The subsequent death of Maricarmen, as the woman became known, caused even more indignation and solidified her as a symbol of Spaniards who feel they pay too much on rent and can’t even dream of homeownership.
Housing activists leveraged the uproar over Maricarmen's eviction to call for the general strike. They soon won the backing of Spain's two main unions, UGT and CCOO.

The housing activists want several measures, including the elimination of tourist apartments, a crackdown on real estate speculation and protection for renters in the form of automatic renewals of leases.
The UGT and CCOO unions are demanding more government intervention in the housing market and a new minimum wage agreement through talks with the business owners' association.
The strike’s official slogan is “Salaries. Housing. Prices.”

The nationwide protests over the eviction of Maricarmen propelled Spain’s government to push through emergency measures to limit evictions and help tenants, but right-wing parties in the Parliament refused to ratify them on the grounds they would provoke a flight of properties from the rental market.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Iran's army said on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) that an oil tanker had struck a mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, where the country has been targeting ships that transit without its authorisation.
Since the outbreak of the West Asia war in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
The United States has, in response, imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.
The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait.

"Early this morning, a violating oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in an unsafe, prohibited area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz," the naval forces of Iran's army said in a statement carried by state TV.
In recent weeks Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships had caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.

U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. military operations in the region, has been escorting ships through the waterway and said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
On Tuesday (November 10), the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said three other oil tankers had caught fire in the strait.

articles.title: Immigration arrests go on unabated despite Trump's misgivings after GOP's midterm wipeout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: It's business as usual for President Donald Trump 's deportation offensive despite the Republican wipeout in the midterm elections.

In Los Angeles, masked immigration officers in body armour blocked a hospital emergency room driveway in a heavily Latino neighbourhood early Saturday (November 7, 2026). In central Alabama, twin 19-year-old brothers from Venezuela were arrested while driving back to college a day after the election.
Advocates reported arrests from California to Michigan to Massachusetts.
After Democrats trounced the GOP and won control of the next Congress, Mr. Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party.
“I'd love to do something on immigration,” he said in an interview with CBS “60 Minutes” recorded Friday (November 6, 2026).

Hours later, he named Stephen Miller , the architect of his hardline immigration agenda, as his new chief of staff. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, meanwhile, said his orders had not changed.

“Deportations will continue,” Mr. Mullin wrote in an online post the day after the election, warning that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement takes no days off and that “this includes on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and Election Day.”
María Bilbao, a campaign coordinator for the American Friends Service Committee in Miami, said she has received at least one call a day from someone detained in South Florida since the election.
“Everything remains exactly the same. The arrests have not ceased at all,” Ms. Bilbao said.

Florida Highway Patrol officers and ICE agents have detained people in their cars, as well as in places including supermarkets, pharmacies and gas stations. Immigrants under supervision have also been arrested when they showed up at ICE's Miami office for their appointments.
Erick Gasca, 31, got home Friday night (November 6, 2026) after an evening playing board games with friends. He lives near Adventist Health White Memorial Medical Center in Los Angeles.
An “unprecedented” number of vehicles with tinted windows and no license plates were parked near the hospital's emergency room entrance, he said.

articles.title: Anaemia prevention in India: pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: India has had decades of unchanged high anaemia prevalence in women and children that has historically been thought to be due to iron deficiency. This has led firstly to an iron and folic acid (IFA) tablet supplementation targeted at women and children, and secondly to fitful implementation of mandatory fortification of staple foods. IFA is a ‘precision’ strategy, applying as it does to the vulnerable population it is intended for, while fortification is a broad strategy that applies to the entire population. The latter works in controlled settings such as clinical trials, but has not worked in real-world settings, and might have adverse effects when given to those it is unintended for.

The reason for pivoting: anaemia is mistakenly conflated with iron deficiency In India. The evidence is otherwise: in national Indian surveys, it has been shown that iron deficiency is not the major cause of anaemia. Indeed, fully one-third of anaemia cases demonstrate no micronutrient deficiency or obvious cause. Even so, giving iron should have sorted out those who did have iron deficiency anaemia, and reduced the general anaemia prevalence. While this could be a problem with inefficient programme implementation, two important questions arise: is there is really a deficiency in dietary iron intake in India? And is the administered iron being adequately absorbed and utilised for haemoglobin formation?

articles.title: Firecrackers still Delhi’s top pollutant after Deepavali, IITM finds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Firecrackers emerged as the biggest contributor to Delhi's air pollution on both Monday (November 9, 2026) and Tuesday (November 10), accounting for 71.1% and 29.8% of the pollution load, respectively, according to source-apportionment estimates by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM).

The contribution of firecrackers to the city's pollution levels was significantly higher on Monday (November 9), a day after Deepavali, before declining on Tuesday (November 11), the IITM models showed.

The estimates had a standard deviation (SD) of 104.1 percentage points on Monday (November 9) and 27.7 percentage points on Tuesday (November 10), indicating considerable variability and uncertainty in the modelled contributions.

On Monday (November 9), vehicular emissions accounted for 6.9% of the pollution, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols at 5% and secondary organic aerosols at 4.5%. Mixed or unresolved biofuel contributed 4.45%, while mineral dust and ash and mixed combustion accounted for 2.5% each.

Wood burning contributed 1.3%, while waste burning, including municipal and plastic-rubber-containing waste, accounted for 1.1%. Coal combustion and industrial emissions contributed 0.5% and 0.2%, respectively.
On Tuesday (November 10), the contribution of firecrackers dropped to 29.8%, while secondary organic aerosols emerged as the second-largest contributor at 17.5%.
Vehicular emissions and secondary inorganic aerosols each accounted for 11.7% of the pollution load, while wood burning contributed 10.7% and waste burning 7.7%.
Vehicular emissions emerged as the third largest contributor to pollution on Tuesday (November 10).
Mixed combustion accounted for 5.1%, followed by mixed or unresolved biofuel at 3.3% and mineral dust and ash at 1.5%.
Delhi's average 24-hour Air Quality Index (AQI) had improved marginally to the 'poor' category on Tuesday (November 10), with the 4 p.m. reading settling at 299.
However, air quality deteriorated again on Wednesday (November 11), with the AQI climbing to 312, placing it in the 'very poor' category.
An AQI between 201 and 300 is classified as 'poor', while readings between 301 and 400 fall in the 'very poor' category.

fullParagraphs: Meta’s new head of WhatsApp, Kunal Shah, has promised simplified calls/messages and more financial services on the messaging platform, apart from increased AI integration.
In a post on the social media platform X on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), Mr. Shah said he had spent around four months at WhatsApp.
He also shared some largely expected goals for the platform.
The WhatsApp executive said he would make voice notes, groups, stickers and video “simpler and more expressive.”

The company is also working with financial services and telecom partners to explore processes such as paying bills, borrowing money, and ensuring connectivity during travel. The aim of this step is to keep users within the messaging platform, even if they are completing other personal finance tasks.
Not surprisingly, Mr. Shah said he wanted to make these features more efficient with AI.
He did not announce any specific features or share a release date for the same.
WhatsApp handles over 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls every day, he shared, while stressing that the company’s principles would not change any time soon.

“Your personal messages and calls stay end-to-end encrypted. This and our quality bar stays the same. What happens inside WhatsApp only matters for what it makes possible outside it: more time together, stronger communities, and fewer barriers between people and the lives they want to live,” shared Mr. Shah.

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

The church sees the initiative as more than a fitness facility. “We want to groom a healthy generation. Many people suffer from lifestyle diseases, while youngsters often turn to private fitness centres. We felt that providing basic facilities here would benefit the community. Spirituality is also about nurturing a healthy mind and body. We consider this a form of spiritual service,” says assistant vicar Fr. Jees Akkara.

For Fr. Eluvathingal, there is another purpose. “Youngsters rarely come to church or participate in its activities these days. This is also an opportunity to bring more of them into the church community,” he says.

articles.title: How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Extramarital affairs are usually private matters. Jensen Huang 's has global implications.

The 63-year-old is the leading face of the artificial intelligence revolution with his black leather jacket and fluff of grey hair. He runs the company Nvidia, which produces highly coveted computer chips. That's landed him on a late-night phone call with President Donald Trump , a promoter of the industry.

But Mr. Huang was also liaising with a Chinese businesswoman who has allegedly fed intelligence — as well as advanced chips — to China. The woman, Alice Huang, is a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed.

It's a saga of personal betrayal, corporate espionage and high-tech development, and the fallout is spreading across Washington. There are bipartisan calls for investigations on Capitol Hill. The U.S. Department of Justice has opened its own probe. Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, is conducting an internal review.

Some expect the technology to reshape human civilisation by imbuing computers with the vast powers of creation and analysis, and Mr. Trump has repeated that “whoever wins AI, wins." Nvidia is the backbone of America's plans for dominating the field.
When asked about Mr. Huang's affair, Mr. Trump said this week that he had spoken to the tech executive as the scandal grew.
“I think he'll be in good shape," President Trump said, adding that "he said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”
As for when the President first learned about the concerns involving Ms. Alice Huang, Mr. Trump brushed off the question.
“They could have been mentioned," he said. "Certainly it didn't make much of an impact on me.”
With the AI race between the U.S. and China often framed as a fierce and consequential rivalry , the Justice Department has persistently warned of the espionage threat posed by Beijing.
That includes efforts to cultivate well-placed relationships in government and private industry, as well as to acquire sensitive technology, such as U.S.-developed AI chips.

Last year, Megaspeed faced scrutiny from the U.S. Commerce Department over allegations that it skirted U.S. export laws and routed a large number of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese users. The company denied those allegations. U.S. intelligence officials eventually concluded that Ms. Alice Huang had spied for China, according to The New York Times.

articles.title: Himalayas agenda left off COP31 formal list as major blocs withhold support: Nepal Foreign Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: An agenda item on the Himalayas proposed by Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan has not been included in the formal list of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) after failing to secure the backing of the developed nations.
The COP 31 commenced on Monday (November 9, 2026) in Antalya, Turkiye. Agenda items refer to the list of topics that are formally taken up for discussion at the conference every year.

Speaking to PTI at COP31, Shisir Khanal, Nepal's Minister of Foreign Affairs, said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that the three countries would continue to face challenges in getting the issue formally recognised without the support of major countries.
He said some nations explicitly backed the proposal raised on Monday (November 9, 2026), while others remained reluctant.

“This is part of a big negotiation. Different major blocs did not support it, and that made it difficult for the agenda to go through. From our side, we pushed as hard as we could. There were different voices in the room. Some explicitly supported our agenda, while others were quite reluctant,” he said.
A source with direct knowledge of the discussions said developed nations did not show interest when the three countries formally pushed the proposal.

“The agenda focused on the Himalayas was clearly diluted, and it was the European Union which did not show any interest in this agenda. Even though the issue is not completely off the charts, a high-level dialogue is expected on it soon,” the source told PTI on condition of anonymity.
The source added that developing nations did not object to or block the proposal when it was raised.

Asked which countries supported the proposal, Mr. Khanal said several Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and mountain nations were positive, while developed countries were reluctant to take up a new agenda.

According to the Nepal government, a research dialogue is expected during the upcoming sessions at COP31, and the presidency has assured that a final text addressing mountain-related issues will be included in the conference's outcome document.

“Compared to the past, we feel there is positive momentum, with the world community increasingly seeing the mountain issue as one of the core issues. That recognition is building. It may take some time to get where we really want to be, but we feel we are on a positive track,” Mr. Khanal said.

Asked why Nepal was emphasising the 1.5 degrees Celsius temperature overshoot in its proposal, Khanal said there was an urgent need to understand the consequences as global temperatures approach that threshold.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. Tel Aviv must take urgent steps to restore its international standing. Third, Israel must reopen the path to peace. The new government should initiate negotiations with the Palestinians under international mediation, crack down on settler violence, pull back from Gaza and reaffirm its commitment to the two-state solution. Without peace, Israel risks continuing to “descend to dark places”.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Government plans curbs on film promotions and commercial events in educational institutions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The government is considering a ban on film promotions and other commercial activities on the premises of educational institutions following a series of incidents involving unauthorised events and alleged safety lapses.

The government is examining the activities that educational institutions can legally conduct on their campuses and those that should be prohibited. Senior officials of the Education department have been asked to prepare guidelines to regulate such activities.

The proposed guidelines are expected to restrict the use of educational institution premises for non-academic, political film promotions and unrelated commercial events. The move comes amid allegations that some private educational institutions have been using students for political and other purposes.

In recent times, some colleges not only declared a holiday to facilitate film promotion events but also recommended students to watch those films. Such practices have also drawn criticism from educationists.

The concern has been compounded by incidents in which students have lost their lives during events organised on institutional premises. In a recent incident, a stage erected for an event at an educational institution collapsed, killing a student and injuring several others.

Under the proposed framework, institutions organising large-scale academic, sports or cultural events may be required to submit advance details to local Education department officials and the police. These would include the expected number of participants, arrangements for stage construction, entry and exit points, crowd management and fire safety measures.

The government is understood to be considering a distinction between minor events intended to encourage students’ sporting, artistic and cultural talents and large gatherings that interfere with academic activities.

Officials point out that the government is keen on activities to promote arts, culture and creativity among students and has over the past three years launched several initiatives to promote skills, employment, innovation and entrepreneurship among them.. However, decision of certain educational institutions to promote particular films and even declare holidays to enable students to watch them has invited criticism from parents and educationists.

articles.title: Bunker Roy, founder of Barefoot College, dies at 81
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: One of the foundational figures of modern civil society in India and the founder of Barefoot College, Sanjit “Bunker” Roy, died at his home in Tilonia, in Rajasthan’s Ajmer district, on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) morning. He was 81.

“He went peacefully as he wanted to in his own home in Tilonia, surrounded by Aruna and some of the countless people who loved and cared for him deeply, passionately,” said a statement issued by the Social Work and Research Centre (SWRC) – Barefoot College.

He was 21 years old when famine struck Bihar in 1966. Consecutive monsoons had failed. Seeing the horrors of extreme poverty, with people dropping dead of starvation, changed the course of his life, and he decided to spurn the “whole world laid out for him”.

Bunker Roy's activism began at a time when social work was often viewed with disdain. His wife and prominent activist, Aruna Roy, recalls in her memoir, The Personal is Political, that when she was serving as a sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) in Delhi, a chief metropolitan magistrate reacted dismissively after learning that Bunker Roy was a social worker. “ Kahin naukri nahin mili hogi (He must not have landed a job anywhere),” her colleague quipped. The magistrate’s attitude changed dramatically, however, when he later discovered that Bunker Roy was the national squash champion, and promptly sought Roy's help in securing membership to the prestigious Delhi Gymkhana Club.

Roy studied at the Doon School alongside future Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and attended St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, between 1962 and 1967. He won the national squash championship in 1965 and represented India in three world championships. In a TED Talk posted online 15 years ago, he described his elite education as “snobbish” and “expensive”, saying it had “almost destroyed” him.

In 1972, Roy founded the Social Work and Research Centre in Tilonia, Rajasthan, which later became widely known as Barefoot College. In the same TED Talk, he described it as “a place for cop-outs, drop-outs and wash-outs” and not for certificate chasers. It had a bottom-up approach, enabling the villagers to “identify their own challenges, develop local solutions and manage their resources independently”, working towards community-based water management and renewable energy initiatives.

Paying tribute, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said Roy’s vision of training rural grandmothers as “Barefoot Solar Engineers” had helped bring electricity to thousands of off-grid homes across India and other developing countries, while advancing community empowerment and environmental stewardship.

Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh recalled Roy as a jovial figure whose love of chocolates earned opprobrium from Mr. Ramesh’s wife for polishing off an entire box without sharing. Mr. Ramesh said Roy believed that civil society “must cooperate where they can, collaborate where they should, and confront where they must". Roy, he said, worked closely with the Rajiv Gandhi government in areas such as drinking water, immunisation, and adult literacy.
Sam Pitroda, who served as an adviser to Rajiv Gandhi and worked with Roy, remembered him as an “institution-builder” whose impact extended far beyond the communities he served.
Former Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot said Roy made significant contributions to rural self-reliance, education, and development while drawing inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi’s principles.
CPI general secretary D. Raja described Roy as a pioneering social activist and educationist whose work would continue to inspire those committed to equality, dignity, and social justice.

Writer Amitav Ghosh noted that despite opportunities to pursue a distinguished career in diplomacy, the bureaucracy, or the corporate world, Roy chose instead to dedicate his life to addressing rural poverty, calling him “a true hero”.

articles.title: Juvenile traced to Srinagar for sending fake Delhi Police notices targeting IFF, SFLC X accounts; Crime Branch registers FIR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Delhi Police’s Crime Branch has registered a case over fraudulent notices purportedly issued in the name of the force, seeking the removal of social media posts and the blocking of accounts belonging to the Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) and the Software Freedom Law Centre (SFLC), an official close to the development told The Hindu.
A juvenile has been traced to Srinagar in connection with the impersonation, sources said.
The FIR has been registered on charges of impersonating a public servant and forgery under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Section 66 of Information Technology (IT) Act.

The development comes days after social media platform X told the Delhi High Court that an internal investigation had established that the notices were not genuine police communications and had been sent by an “imposter”. The platform also told the court that it had not acted on the requests and would not take down the organisations’ accounts.

The case follows a November 6 hearing before Justice Amit Mahajan, who was hearing petitions filed by the two digital rights organisations challenging the purported takedown requests. X’s counsel told the court that the platform had conducted an internal investigation and found that someone had impersonated the Delhi Police.
“We did not act on it. Notices are not sent by the Delhi Police. We have filed a complaint with the Delhi Police last night to find the imposter,” X’s counsel submitted.
The court recorded the platform’s assurance and disposed of the petitions, granting the organisations liberty to approach it again if any action was taken against their accounts.

The controversy began after X forwarded two purported ‘Illegal Content Reports’ to IFF on November 3. The first, dated October 31, sought the removal of a post published by IFF on October 30 and another post by SFLC. The second, dated November 2, sought the removal of 37 posts and the blocking of three accounts — @internetfreedom, @SFLCin and @geoblockedindia — in their entirety.

The notices alleged that the posts were “defamatory” towards the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). They reportedly called for the content to be removed or withheld within three hours, citing provisions of the Information Technology Act and the IT Rules, 2021.

IFF had said that the posts in question reproduced and commented on a legal notice purportedly sent to the organisation on behalf of the RSS. It maintained that the posts constituted protected speech under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution and that it had not been given prior notice before the takedown requests were submitted.
The organisation subsequently served a legal notice on the Delhi Police and X Corp. through its counsel, seeking clarification over the requests.

SFLC, meanwhile, had questioned the authenticity of the communications after attempting to verify them with the Delhi Police. It said an email sent to the address mentioned in the purported notices was returned as undelivered, with an error stating that the user did not exist. The organisation pointed out that the same email address was listed on the Delhi Police website at the time, further raising questions about the communications.

articles.title: Akhilesh to visit Ram Temple; promises to transform Ayodhya into capital of Sanatan pilgrimage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A war of words has erupted over the Samajwadi Party (SP) president and former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav’s plan to visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on December 12. This would be his first visit since its consecration in January 2024.

Making a statement on Tuesday, the Uttar Pradesh BJP president, Pankaj Chaudhary, challenged Mr. Yadav to visit the Temple on December 6 — anniversary of the Babri Masjid demolition — and apologise for the killing of kar sevaks during SP rule.

“If this is true repentance and not a new trick on Lord Shri Ram, visit the Temple on 6th December, not 12th. Hundreds of devotees were murdered. Apologize for that sin. Do not think that your past sins will be washed away,” wrote Mr. Chaudhary, on X.

Amid the uproar Mr. Yadav promised to make Ayodhya the global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage. “We are committed to restoring the honor and dignity of Ayodhya. We will improve and enhance it so the number of visitors to Ayodhya is boosted. Their numbers have been dwindling due to the theft at the Temple, which has directly impacted the local economy. We will also strive to restore trust by providing a transparent system. By building world-class infrastructure, we will make Ayodhya the ‘global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage’,” Mr. Yadav wrote on X.

The SP president went on to add, “We will build an Ayodhya where no arrogant person insults or harasses a poor woman or child collecting a little oil, and beats them with a cane. We will regain power and fulfill the nutritional needs of our citizens by providing oil and ghee. We will promote traditional boating so the boatmen can benefit and the strong bond between Lord Ram and the Nishadraj can be re-established. The BJP is trying to break this connection; it seeks to use its hegemony to ensure no one remembers the close ties Lord Ram and the PDA community shared.”

“We will free Ayodhya from outside contractors and initiate a land investigation. Outsiders have looted Ayodhya. None of the BJP leaders and corrupt officials involved in the circle rate scam will be spared. Their coffers, filled with the loot from Ayodhya, will be emptied. We will establish a system to ensure no evil-minded person can insult — or walk free after insulting — not just Lord Ram or Lord Krishna but also the deities and great men of other faiths. Such individuals will be legally detained. Those who harbour such unrighteous individuals who use abusive language are also partners in sin; they too will be punished for their involvement in the conspiracy to disrupt social harmony,” added the SP chief.

articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players.

“Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.”

The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.

One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

Industry experts also suggest that while amendments in tax laws are just one part of attracting inflows, what remains important is continued momentum in corporate earnings growth, policy certainty and a stable rupee.

As such, simplifying onboarding and setting one predictable tax clearance process at exit coupled with making dispute resolution faster and binding is what would bring stable long-term investments, Nangia noted.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.
